hepatitis B virus ( HBV ) infects normal hepastic stem/progenitor cell s ( NSC s) but in the short-term does not appear to alter those NSC characteristics that are associated with the development of chronic liver disease ( CLD ) and/or hepatocelluar carcinoma ( HCC ).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this pilot study do not suggest that HBV infections of NSCs contribute to HBV induced CLD or HCC.
HBV infect NSCs but in this study, the infection did not alter NSC activities that might be associated with the development of CLDs or HCCs.

HBV infect normal hepatic stem cells and such infections are associated with a lack of changes in the NSC pro inflammatory, membrane PD, proliferative and telomerases activities that have been associated with the development of CLDs and HCCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HBV infection of NSCs is not likely to contribute to HBV induced liver injury or the development of CLDs or HCC.
NSCs are infected by HBV, but that the infection has no immediate effect on the NSC activity.
HBV infect normal hepatic stem cells, but the infection does not alter the activity of these cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NSCs of the liver are not a major reservoir for the hepatitis B virus.
HBV infection of human NSCs is a common event but that such infections are unlikely to contribute to the pathogenesis of CLD and HCC.
HBV infect normal hepatic stem cells, which are known to be present in the normal liver.
